transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Doc. Uh, well, they said I needed to come see you because... because my talking gets all mixed up lately. Like, I'll be trying to explain something simple, right? Like about the keys. I clean buildings, so I got this big ring of keys, heavy on the belt, and they jingle. Sounds just like a jail guard when I walk down the halls. 

Which makes me think about the jail, and I try to explain about the jail to people, but then my mind just goes right over to... to this prayer rug. I saw a really beautiful prayer rug once, deep red, with these gold fringes on the end. And the patterns on it, they looked exactly like chess pieces. I don't even play chess much anymore, not since the ninth grade anyway. The knight is the tricky one because it jumps, you know? But I start talking about the prayer rug and the chess pieces, and... what was I saying? 

Oh, right. Yeah, people just tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. They say I jump around too much.
Have you been feeling unusually energetic, like you don't need much sleep, or have you been feeling extremely low or hopeless lately?

Well, energetic... yeah, I guess you could say that. I mean, I'll lay down for maybe two, three hours, tops. And then my eyes just pop open, way before the sun even thinks about coming up. I feel completely fresh, like I've slept a whole weekend. And I just start planning out all the things I need to do at work, mapping out the floors in my head. It's like sleep is just this thing other people need, you know? Not me. 

Speaking of the sun coming up, though... have you ever really watched the sunrise from a high window? The building I clean, on the top floor, there's this one window facing east. And when the light hits the glass, it turns this crazy shade of orange. Not like a regular orange, but like the color of those old traffic cones they used to have back in the day. The really heavy rubber ones that smelled like tar if you got too close. I remember smelling tar when they were paving the street outside my house when I was a kid. The machines were so loud, rumbling the whole house... but yeah, I don't really need much sleep at all.
Do you ever feel like you are receiving special messages from things you see or hear, or do you ever hear voices that other people around you cannot hear?

Voices... yeah, actually. It's usually when I'm at work, late at night when the building's mostly empty. I'll be near the vents, or sometimes right by the mop closet on the third floor, and I'll hear this man's voice. He says my name, or he tells me I ruined everything. And Doc, it sounds as real as you sitting right there. It echoes a bit, you know? 

Like the way sound bounces around in an empty parking garage. I used to park my car in this underground garage downtown, back when I had that old Chevy. Man, that car was a boat. The suspension was shot, so every time you went over a speed bump, it felt like you were on a roller coaster. I loved roller coasters when I was a kid. The wooden ones, mostly. They rattle your teeth right out of your head, but there's something about the smell of the old wood and the grease on the tracks... 

Anyway, the voice. Yeah. It's just this man, telling me I ruined it all, clear as day.
Have there been times in the past when you were sleeping normally and your mood was stable, yet you were still hearing these voices?

Yeah, actually. There have been times like that. Like, I remember a few weeks... maybe a month ago? I was sleeping fine, you know, a solid seven or eight hours. Wasn't feeling all revved up, wasn't feeling down in the dumps either. Just... normal, I guess. But I still heard him. For more than two weeks, I was still hearing that guy in the vents, telling me I ruined it. And I was also convinced the people working late in the offices were tapping on their desks to send signals about me. 

Speaking of desks, some of these offices have those really nice, heavy mahogany ones. You don't see wood like that much anymore. It reminds me of this old cabinet my grandmother used to have in her dining room. She kept all her good china in there, the plates with the little blue flowers painted around the edges. We were never allowed to touch them, only on Thanksgiving. Thanksgiving was always a big deal at her house. The smell of the turkey roasting would hit you before you even opened the front door... but yeah, I was feeling totally fine mood-wise, sleeping regular, but still hearing the voice and seeing the signals for a couple of weeks there.
